Disposal of pending cases by retired judges 
*401. SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO: Will the Minister of 
LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a group of retired judges of Patna High Court has 
offered to return to the bench to assist the court to dispose of over 
100,000 pending cases; and 
(b) if so, Government's response in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY 
AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): (a) and (b) The Bihar Retired 
High Court Judges Society, in their meeting held on 20.1.2002, 
resolved to offer assistance in early disposal of pending cases in  the  
Patna High  Court.  A copy  of this resolution  has

been forwarded to the Union Government as well as the Hon'bl Chief 
Justice of India and the Hon'ble Chief Justice of the Patiu High Court. 
It is for the Patna High Court to take a view in the matter. 
As per the available figures, the number of cases pending in the 
Patna High Court was 80,956 as on 31.12.2001. 
The Judge strength of each High Court is reviewed, every 3 years, 
taking into account certain parameters including the institution and the 
backlog of cases. The last such review was done in 1999 and the next 
review in respect of all High Courts, including Patna High Court, is 
due during the current year. 
Facilities in Hospitals 
*402. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of 
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news-
item captioned "Facilities in hospitals  exist only on paper: panel", 
which appeared in the Hindu, dated the 18th March, 2002; 
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto; and 
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to implement the 
recommendations of the Parliament ary Committee to provide quality 
medical facilities in the various me dical institutes and hospitals of 
Government? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. 
C.P. THAKUR): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Press Report has referred to 
the recommendations of Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Human Resource Development. A statement indicating 
the status on the points raised in the Press Report is enclosed. 
2 

[22 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement  
Status of the points raised in Press Report 
1. Non-Functional Equipments:—  
Monthly review/monitoring of stat us of non-functional equipments 
costing more than Rs. 1.00 lakh in respect of Central Government 
Hospitals is being undertaken at the Directorate General of Health 
Services. Most of the costly and vital equipments are placed under 
Annual Maintenance Contracts. The reasons for any equipment being 
non-functional are normal wear and t ear and use of the equipments. 
As on date, in the Central Govern ment hospitals (Dr. Ram Manohar 
Lohia Hospital; Safdarjung Hospital; Associated Hospitals of Lady 
Hardinge Medical College), out of 838 equipment of a value above 
Rs. 1 lakh each, only 6 are non-functional. 
2. Coordination between Hospitals:—  
A nodal officer is designated in the emergency control room of each 
hospital. The emergency control r oom is manned by Chief Medical 
Officer/Senior Medical Officer round the clock to attend and 
coordinate the treatment facilities required for the serious patients 
coming to the casualty. Besides, a senior officer takes an evening 
round to oversee the arrangement of the casualty and emergency 
facilities in each of the hospital. 
A proper referral system of treatm ent and follow-up already exists 
between Safdarjung Hospital and A ll India Institute of Medical 
Sciences (AIIMS). In emergency cases, Hospital Administrations has 
been communicating and coordinating regularly for referring of 
patients from AIlRlS casualty to Safdarjung Hospital and similarly 
from Safdarjung Hospital to AIIMS. If need be. Further, coordination 
is also being maintained as regard s the major investigative procedures 
like CT, MRI etc. in case such equipments are out of order in any of 
these hospitals. 
 3. Increase in Patients with no increase in number of beds:—  
There is a considerable increase in the number of OPD and indoor 
patients in Central Government Hospitals. 47 indoor beds in Dr. RML 
Hospital and 51 beds in LHMC and Associated Hospitals have been 
increased in the Ninth Five Year Plan. For reducing the waiting 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [22 April, 2002] 
time, more registration counters are run during the rush hours. In 
LHMC, number of registration counters have been increased from 4 to 
6 and in Safdarjung Hospital from 6 to 14. Besides, 14 to 18 special 
clinics are run in Dr. RML Hospital. Safdarjung Hospital and LHMC 
and Associated Hospital in the afternoon. 
To cope with the patients rush , AIIMS is expanding its hospital 
services in specialities like Dr. R.P. Centre, C.T. Centre, Neuro-
Sciences Centre etc. It is also pr oposed to have a screening OPD near 
to the present OPD building. 
Keeping in view the large patient-load, the Government of NCT of 
Delhi has constructed/commissi oned/upgraded 15 hospitals/Trauma 
Centers (9 Peripheral hospitals, 4 existing major hospitals and 2 
Trauma Centers) during the Ninth Five Year Plan i.e. 1997—2002. 
Seven new hospitals and one dental  college building at Lok Nayak 
Hospital Complex are under constr uction, eight hospitals are under 
expansion and three colony hospita ls are under upgradation. Land for 
five hospitals has been purchased and the facilities are under 
planning/SFC stage. Construction of these hospitals is to start during 
2002-2003. 
4. Overcrowding adversely  affecting  research  activities in  AIIMS, 
PGI Chandigarh and JIPMER Pondicherry:—  
Despite the burden of patients, AIIMS has been rated as the top 
Institution in clinical, medical and bio-medical research in the 
country. The specific measures fo r encouraging research activities 
include:—  
(i) Identification of priority areas of research. 
(ii) Increasing Plan Outlay on research. 
(iii) Revamping the Scheme/Research Cell: 
The function and working of the research/scheme cell has 
already been reviewed and the same is being revamped in 
order to respond to the challenges of the new millennium. 
4 

[22 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
(iv) Creation of an advanced centre for Molecular Medicine 
during the Tenth Plan period:—  
An advanced centre for Molecular Medicine is being 
planned for development molecular diagnostics and 
therapeutics, cell and tissue engineering, progeonics and 
genomics, transplantati on immunology, molecular 
epidemology, new drug discovery and bioinformatics. This 
centre is expected to give a real boost to research in 
AIIMS. 
In PGIMER, Chandigarh, during the Ninth Five Year Plan with a view 
to boost medical education and resear ch activities, various measures 
had been taken which include the following:—  
(i) Upgradation of various departments. 
(ii) To develop new Centres, namely, Advanced Cardiac Centre, 
Advanced Eye Centre, Advanc ed Trauma Centre, Bone 
Marrow Transplant Centre and 2nd phase of Advanced 
Paediatrics Centre 
The PGI is trying its best to carry out the research work, which is one 
of the basic objectives of the Institute and over 400 research papers are 
published from the Institute every year. The Institute has a separate fund 
of its own for sanction of Institute Research Projects to the Faculty 
Members. The Institute also en courages and motivates the Faculty 
Members of seek funding from National/International Agencies for their 
research projects i.e. D.S.T. (Govt, of India), D.B.T. (Govt, of India), 
C.S.I.R., New Delhi, ICMR, New Delhi and the W.H.O. etc. etc. 
JIPMER, Pondicherry is also undertaking similar initiatives to boost 
the research activities in the institute. 
5. Screening OPD at AIIMS:—  
The new Master Layout Plan for screening OPD of AIIMS has been 
prepared and the same has been subm itted to concerned authorities for 
their approval. It is expected that the construction work shall start by 
September 2002.

6. Computerization  of OPD  Registration  in  Central government 
Hospitals:—  
The computerization of various de partments in Safdarjung Hospital 
has been started. Computerizati on has been started in Dr. RML 
Hospital and LHMC and Associated Hospital for Administration and 
Medical Stores. A proposal for comput erization of all services in Dr. 
RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and LHMC and Associated 
Hospital is under process. 
Computerization of patient care system at AIIMS has been entrusted 
to consultant and the consultant has already submitted their report. 
Based on the reports, tenders for co mputerization have already been 
floated. It is expected that the pa tient care system of AIIMS will be 
fully computerized within 2 years of  finalisation of tenders. Adequate 
funds are available for computerization. 
7. Separate  Queues  for Senior  Citizens  in  Central government 
Hospitals:—  
A provision for separate queue for priority treatment to senior 
citizen patients is already in ex istence in the OPD of Central 
Government Hospitals. 
8. Cleanliness and hygiene and lack of coordination between Local 
Bodies and Hospital Authorities:—  
Senior level Medical Officers have been made responsible for 
overseeing the cleanliness of hospital premises. The premises have 
been divided into zones and r esponsibility assigned to Sanitary 
Inspectors for the upkeep of the premises and laboratories. Hospitals 
arrange cleanliness drives periodically. Incinerators are being used for 
the disposal of bilogical waste like dead foetus, etc. and other infected 
waste including physical material lik e syringes, needles, bottles etc. 
As regards non-infected, non-hazardous waste, the NDMOlocal 
bodies are responsible for its coll ection and disposal. The hospital 
authorities have been liaising with local bodies for disposal of this 
waste. The matter is also being taken up in the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests to bring the problem into focus and give a 
direction to the hospitals, local bodies and other engaged

in the task of hospital waste manage ment. Adequate attention is being 
paid by LHMC for the management of hospital waste. The cleanliness 
and hygiene of the hospital is being improved and wherever 
necessary, renovation of toilets has been undertaken. Under the 
Comprehensive Redevelopment Plan, proposals for latest amenities for 
sewerage, water supply and management of hospital waste have been 
incorporated. 
9. Creation of an 'Ombudsman' Type of machinery:—  
A public grievances committee has been functioning in each of the 
Central Government hospital for looking into the complaints of 
patients and there is a public grievances committee in the Dte. GHS 
headed by the D.G. A citizen charter is also in existence in each of the 
Central Government Hospital.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH 
AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) Under the 
provisions of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules thereunder, 
State Government have been empowered to enforce quality of durgs 
including check on manufacture or sale of spurious and banned drugs. 
The said Act was amended in 1982 to provide for specific definition 
of spurious drug. Manufacture and sale of spurious drug, if detected, 
is punishable with imprisonment fo r a term which may extend to a 
term of the life and with fine

RAJYA SABHA [22 April, 2002] 
which shall not be less than Rs. 10,000/-. Hence there are adequate

Section 26-A of the said Act empowers Central Government to 
prohibit manufacture, sale or distribution of drugs whose use is likely 
to involve any risk to any human being or it does not have the 
therapeutic value claimed or does not have therapeutic justification. 
72 categories of drugs have already been prohibited by the 
Government. The Act provides one year imprisonment but which may 
extend to two years and fine if any person is found contravening the 
provision of manufacture, sale or distribution of prohibited drug. 
(d) Since manufacture and sale of spurious medicine is a clandestine

(ii) Establishment of separate intelligence-cum-legal machinery 
with police assistance.

prosecution etc. in respect of spurious counterfeit drugs.

procedures.
